question.question:
A retailer time-weights average inventory: each balance is weighted by the whole months it is held in the 12-month year, and the weighted sum is divided by 12. Standalone inventory is 630000 USD in months 1-6; a seasonal adjustment of 10000 USD (added algebraically; negative means a reduction) applies in months 7-12. Standalone cost of goods sold for the year is 5000000 USD. On the first day of month 6 the retailer acquires a business holding 350000 USD of inventory, held at that level for the rest of the year and incurring cost of goods sold of 180000 USD per month after closing. Policy: if closing is in month 6 or earlier, the acquired inventory enters the time-weighted average for the months held and its post-closing cost of goods sold is added to consolidated cost of goods sold; if closing is in month 7 or later, both are excluded entirely as non-comparable. Inventory turnover is cost of goods sold used divided by average inventory; days inventory on hand is 365 days divided by turnover. Compute days inventory on hand.

Answer format: use exact arithmetic through all intermediate steps, round only the final value half up to 2 decimal digits, and return only the numeric value interpreted in `days` with no unit label or additional text.
